name: Malchijah
overview: Malchijah is a male figure mentioned in Scripture as a descendant of Parosh who had married a foreign wife. Specific tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in the biblical text. His mention highlights a particular instance of intermarriage addressed during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Malchijah means 'YHWH is [my] king,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges God's sovereign kingship. This proper name is recorded in Ezra 10:25 and was not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Malchijah as a descendant of Parosh, establishing a genealogical connection. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Malchijah's significance lies in his representation of the challenges faced by the returning exiles who had intermarried with foreign wives, a practice that was addressed to maintain covenantal purity. His mention in Ezra 10:25 serves to illustrate the community's efforts to realign with God's commands during the restoration period. Through his example, the narrative emphasizes faithfulness to God's covenant as central to Israel's identity and restoration.
